  • Cup feeding: Cup feeding involves offering milk or formula to the child in a small cup, allowing them to lap or sip the liquid. Cup feeding may be appropriate for children on CPAP who are able to swallow safely and tolerate oral feeding.
  • IV fluids: Intravenous (IV) fluids are not typically used as a method of feeding unless absolutely necessary, such as in cases where oral or enteral feeding is not feasible or contraindicated. IV fluids are primarily used for fluid resuscitation or to provide hydration and nutrition when oral or enteral feeding is not possible or inadequate. In the case of a hemodynamically stable child on CPAP, IV fluids are unlikely to be the best method of feeding unless there are specific indications for their use.

So, while nasogastric feeding (option b) may be a suitable method of providing nutrition to a child on CPAP, the choice of feeding method should be based on the child's individual needs, condition, and ability to feed safely. • Burns are not usually linked to hypokalemia, or low potassium levels. Actually, because burns cause injured cells to leak potassium into the circulation, electrolyte abnormalities like hyperkalemia—high potassium levels—are more frequently linked to burns. Burn is therefore not the appropriate response.
  • Increased uric acid shows no clear correlation between potassium and uric acid levels. The breakdown of purines produces uric acid as a waste product, and elevated levels of this acid are frequently linked to diseases like gout or other metabolic problems. It does not, however, directly affect the body's potassium levels. Consequently, raising uric acid is the wrong choice.         
  • Addison's disease, also known as adrenal insufficiency, is typified by a reduction in the synthesis of adrenal hormones, such as aldosterone, which is involved in the regulation of potassium. It is therefore erroneous because Addison's illness is linked to high potassium levels rather than low potassium levels.  
  • Nasogastric suction procedure includes inserting a tube via the nose into the stomach to remove contents. Loss of digestive enzymes, potassium, and stomach acid can result from this procedure. Since potassium is a significant electrolyte present in gastric fluid, the loss of potassium-rich gastric contents during prolonged nasogastric suction can lead to hypokalemia. Given that nasogastric suction is a known cause of hypokalemia, it is the appropriate response.

However, do not induce vomiting or administer anything orally, as this may exacerbate the situation.

Other choices are incorrect as:

  • Gastric Lavage: Gastric lavage (stomach pumping) is generally not recommended for the management of kerosene ingestion, especially in children, due to the risk of aspiration and further complications. It is not considered a standard treatment in this scenario.

choices.title: Abruptio placenta
choices.correct_explanation:
• Given the symptoms described, the condition most likely to be suspected is abruptio placenta.
  • Abruptio placenta, also known as placental abruption, is a serious obstetric complication characterized by the premature separation of the placenta from the uterine wall before delivery. It can result in abdominal pain, tenderness, and fetal distress due to disruption of the placental blood supply, leading to decreased oxygen and nutrient delivery to the fetus.
  • Symptoms of abruptio placenta can vary depending on the extent of placental separation and may include abdominal pain or tenderness, vaginal bleeding (which may be concealed if the blood is trapped behind the placenta), uterine contractions, and signs of fetal distress such as decreased fetal movement or abnormal fetal heart rate patterns.

Options for why the other choices are incorrect:

  • Placenta previa: Placenta previa involves the implantation of the placenta in the lower segment of the uterus, partially or completely covering the cervix. It typically presents with painless vaginal bleeding in the second or third trimester. While fetal distress can occur in severe cases of placenta previa, abdominal pain and tenderness are less common features.
  • Abortion: Abortion refers to the termination of pregnancy before the fetus is viable. While abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding are common symptoms of abortion, fetal distress is not typically associated with abortion in the context described.
  • Ectopic pregnancy: Ectopic pregnancy occurs when a fertilized egg implants outside the uterus, most commonly in the fallopian tube. While ectopic pregnancy can present with abdominal pain and tenderness, as well as signs of intra-abdominal bleeding, it is less likely in a pregnant woman at 32 weeks of gestation, as most ectopic pregnancies are diagnosed earlier in the first trimester. Additionally, fetal distress would not be expected in ectopic pregnancy, as the fetus is not located within the uterus.

  • Mucosal cancer: "Mucosal cancer" is a broad term that can refer to cancers arising from various mucosal surfaces in the body, including the respiratory tract, gastrointestinal tract, and genitourinary tract. Without further information specifying the location of the mucosal cancer, it's difficult to determine its likelihood based solely on the provided information.
  • Uterine cancer: Uterine cancer (endometrial cancer) may present with symptoms such as abnormal uterine bleeding, pelvic pain, or an enlarged uterus on imaging studies. choices.title: Oral
choices.correct_explanation:
Core body temperature refers to the temperature of deep internal tissues (especially hypothalamus, thoracic and abdominal organs). A true core measurement is obtained only from sites that are highly perfused and in close thermal equilibrium with central blood temperature.

  • Rectal temperature is a well-accepted clinical surrogate for core temperature because the rectum is relatively insulated and reflects deep body temperature better than surface sites.
  • Urinary bladder temperature (measured via a thermistor Foley catheter) closely correlates with core temperature because urine temperature reflects blood temperature in the pelvis, especially when urine flow is adequate. This is widely used in ICU and anesthesia monitoring.
  • Temporal artery thermometry estimates core temperature by detecting infrared heat from the temporal artery, which is supplied by the carotid circulation; hence it is designed to approximate central temperature.

Oral temperature is not considered a core temperature method because it is significantly influenced by external and local factors such as:

  • hot/cold drinks
  • mouth breathing
  • oxygen therapy
  • smoking
  • poor probe placement
  • reduced perfusion states

Therefore, oral temperature is categorized as a peripheral / near-core measurement, not a true core measurement.

Distractor 

  • Rectal and urinary bladder are established clinical core-surrogates.
  • Temporal artery is designed to approximate core temperature non-invasively.
  • Oral is too variable and environment-dependent to represent true core temperature.

Once the needle pierces the skin, continue pulling on the skin with the non-dominant hand, and at the same time, grasp the lower end of the syringe barrel with the fingers of the non-dominant hand to stabilize it. Now, move the dominant hand and pull the end of the plunger to aspirate for blood, if indicated. If no blood appears, inject the medication slowly. Once the medication is given, leave the needle in place for ten seconds. After the medication is completely injected, remove the needle using a smooth, steady motion, and then release the skin.   2. The test allows only five attempt, so please take the test carefully.
  3. Test is prepared with a focus on the NORCET exam; therefore, the standard of questions ranges from basic to intermediate.
  4. Each page display one question and to navigate to next question click on next
  5. To review the previous question click on Previous
  6. You can attempt the question in Practice and Exam Mode
  7. In Practice mode you can view the solution at the same time
  8. I exam mode the solution can be seen after submission in review mode

Answering a Question

  1. Each question will have four options, out of which only one must be selected.
  2. You will receive 1 mark for every correct answer, and 0.33 mark (1/3rd) will be deducted for each incorrect answer.
  3. Click the option you want to mark, in case you want to another question simply select another option the first selection will be automatically omitted.
  4. To attempt the next question click on next to attempt the previous Question click on previous
  5. You can bookmark the Question or also report a question
